Chafa
=====

Chafa is a command-line utility that converts image data, including
animated GIFs, into graphics formats or ANSI/Unicode character art suitable
for display in a terminal. It has broad feature support, allowing it to be
used on devices ranging from historical teleprinters to modern terminal
emulators and everything in between.

The core functionality is provided by a C library with a public,
well-documented API.

Both library and frontend tools are covered by the Lesser GPL license,
version 3 or later (LGPLv3+).

For the most up-to-date information, please see https://hpjansson.org/chafa/

Installing with package manager
-------------------------------

Chafa is available as packages for many software distributions. A few are
listed below, along with their command-line installation instructions:

Arch Linux .... pacman -S chafa
Brew .......... brew install chafa
Debian ........ apt install chafa
Fedora ........ dnf install chafa
FreeBSD ....... pkg install chafa
Gentoo ........ emerge media-gfx/chafa
Guix .......... guix install chafa
Kali Linux .... apt install chafa
MacPorts ...... port install chafa
OpenBSD ....... pkg_add chafa
openSUSE ...... zypper in chafa
Ubuntu ........ apt install chafa

On Windows, Chafa can be installed via Scoop and Winget:

Scoop ....... scoop install chafa
Winget ....... winget install hpjansson.Chafa

See https://hpjansson.org/chafa/download/ for more.

Usage
-----

Basic usage:

  chafa [OPTIONS] [IMAGE...]

Common options:

  -s, --size <WxH>        Set output size in character cells
  -c, --colors <mode>     Color mode (2, 16, 240, 256, full, etc.)
  --symbols <symbols>     Select symbol sets for character art output
  --format <format>       Output format (symbols, sixels, kitty, iterm)
  --animate <on|off>      Enable/disable animation
  -d, --duration <secs>   Animation duration
  --bg <color>            Background color
  --fg <color>            Foreground color
  -h, --help              Show help

Examples:

  # Convert an image to terminal art
  chafa image.jpg

  # Set specific output size
  chafa --size 80x25 image.png

  # Animate a GIF
  chafa animation.gif

  # Use Sixel graphics (if terminal supports it)
  chafa --format sixels image.jpg

Language bindings

# Chafa

## About

Chafa is a command-line utility that converts image data, including
animated GIFs, into graphics formats or ANSI/Unicode character art suitable
for display in a terminal. It has broad feature support, allowing it to be
used on devices ranging from historical teleprinters to modern terminal
emulators and everything in between.

The core functionality is provided by a C library with a public,
well-documented API.

Both library and frontend tools are covered by the Lesser GPL license,
version 3 or later (LGPLv3+).

## Features

- Converts images (including animated GIFs) to terminal-displayable formats
- Supports multiple output formats: ANSI/Unicode character art, Sixel graphics, iTerm2 inline images, Kitty graphics protocol
- Works with various terminal types from historical teleprinters to modern emulators
- Handles multiple image formats as input
- Animation support with customizable playback

## Usage

Basic usage:

```sh
chafa [OPTIONS] [IMAGE...]
```

### Common Options

- `-s, --size <WxH>` - Set output size in character cells
- `-c, --colors <mode>` - Color mode (2, 16, 240, 256, full, etc.)
- `--symbols <symbols>` - Select symbol sets for character art output
- `--format <format>` - Output format (symbols, sixels, kitty, iterm)
- `--animate <on|off>` - Enable/disable animation
- `-d, --duration <seconds>` - Animation duration
- `--bg <color>` - Background color
- `--fg <color>` - Foreground color

### Examples

Convert an image to terminal art:
```sh
chafa image.jpg
```

Set specific output size:
```sh
chafa --size 80x25 image.png
```

Animate a GIF with limited duration:
```sh
chafa --duration 10 animation.gif
```

Use Sixel graphics (if terminal supports it):
```sh
chafa --format sixels image.jpg
```

- **Debian/Ubuntu**: `apt install chafa`

- **FreeBSD**: `pkg install chafa`

Chafa
=====

Chafa is a command-line utility that converts image data, including
animated GIFs, into graphics formats or ANSI/Unicode character art suitable
for display in a terminal. It has broad feature support, allowing it to be
used on devices ranging from historical teleprinters to modern terminal
emulators and everything in between.

The core functionality is provided by a C library with a public,
well-documented API.

Both library and frontend tools are covered by the Lesser GPL license,
version 3 or later (LGPLv3+).

For the most up-to-date information, please see https://hpjansson.org/chafa/

Installing with package manager
-------------------------------

Chafa is available as packages for many software distributions. A few are
listed below, along with their command-line installation instructions:

Arch Linux .... pacman -S chafa
Brew .......... brew install chafa
Debian ........ apt install chafa
Fedora ........ dnf install chafa
FreeBSD ....... pkg install chafa
Gentoo ........ emerge media-gfx/chafa
Guix .......... guix install chafa
Kali Linux .... apt install chafa
MacPorts ...... port install chafa
OpenBSD ....... pkg_add chafa
openSUSE ...... zypper in chafa
Ubuntu ........ apt install chafa

On Windows, Chafa can be installed via Scoop and Winget:

Scoop ....... scoop install chafa
Winget ....... winget install hpjansson.Chafa

See https://hpjansson.org/chafa/download/ for more.

Usage
-----

Basic usage:

  chafa [OPTIONS] [IMAGE...]

Common options:

  -s, --size <WxH>        Set output size in character cells
  -c, --colors <mode>     Color mode (2, 16, 240, 256, full, etc.)
  --symbols <symbols>     Select symbol sets for character art output
  --format <format>       Output format (symbols, sixels, kitty, iterm)
  --animate <on|off>      Enable/disable animation
  -d, --duration <secs>   Animation duration
  --bg <color>            Background color
  --fg <color>            Foreground color
  -h, --help              Show help

Examples:

  # Convert an image to terminal art
  chafa image.jpg

  # Set specific output size
  chafa --size 80x25 image.png

  # Animate a GIF
  chafa animation.gif

  # Use Sixel graphics (if terminal supports it)
  chafa --format sixels image.jpg

Language bindings
-----------------

Chafa has bindings for other programming languages:

# Chafa

## About

Chafa is a command-line utility that converts image data, including
animated GIFs, into graphics formats or ANSI/Unicode character art suitable
for display in a terminal. It has broad feature support, allowing it to be
used on devices ranging from historical teleprinters to modern terminal
emulators and everything in between.

The core functionality is provided by a C library with a public,
well-documented API.

Both library and frontend tools are covered by the Lesser GPL license,
version 3 or later (LGPLv3+).

## Features

- Converts images (including animated GIFs) to terminal-displayable formats
- Supports multiple output formats: ANSI/Unicode character art, Sixel graphics, iTerm2 inline images, Kitty graphics protocol
- Works with various terminal types from historical teleprinters to modern emulators
- Handles multiple image formats as input
- Animation support with customizable playback

## Usage

Basic usage:

```sh
chafa [OPTIONS] [IMAGE...]
```

### Common Options

- `-s, --size <WxH>` - Set output size in character cells
- `-c, --colors <mode>` - Color mode (2, 16, 240, 256, full, etc.)
- `--symbols <symbols>` - Select symbol sets for character art output
- `--format <format>` - Output format (symbols, sixels, kitty, iterm)
- `--animate <on|off>` - Enable/disable animation
- `-d, --duration <seconds>` - Animation duration
- `--bg <color>` - Background color
- `--fg <color>` - Foreground color

### Examples

Convert an image to terminal art:
```sh
chafa image.jpg
```

Set specific output size:
```sh
chafa --size 80x25 image.png
```

Animate a GIF with limited duration:
```sh
chafa --duration 10 animation.gif
```

import subprocess, struct, zlib
def write_png(path, w, h, pixels):
    # pixels: list of rows, each row list of (r,g,b,a) or (r,g,b)
    # write RGBA or RGB?
    # Use 8-bit RGB
    def chunk(typ, data):
        c = struct.pack(">I", len(data)) + typ + data
        c += struct.pack(">I", zlib.crc32(typ+data) & 0xffffffff)
        return c
    header = struct.pack(">8s", b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n")
    ihdr = struct.pack(">IIBBBBB", w, h, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0)  # color type 2 = RGB
    # check if need alpha? use 2 for RGB
    raw = b""
    for row in pixels:
        raw += b"\x00"  # filter 0
        for (r,g,b) in row:
            raw += struct.pack("BBB", r,g,b)
    comp = zlib.compress(raw)
    png = header + chunk(b"IHDR", ihdr) + chunk(b"IDAT", comp) + chunk(b"IEND", b"")

def write_png(path, w, h, pixels):
    def chunk(typ, data):
        import struct, zlib
        c = struct.pack(">I", len(data)) + typ + data
        c += struct.pack(">I", zlib.crc32(typ+data) & 0xffffffff)
        return c
    import struct, zlib
    header = struct.pack(">8s", b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n")
    ihdr = struct.pack(">IIBBBBB", w, h, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0)
    raw = b""
    for row in pixels:
        raw += b"\x00"
        for (r,g,b) in row:

    comp = zlib.compress(raw)
    png = header + chunk(b"IHDR", ihdr) + chunk(b"IDAT", comp) + chunk(b"IEND", b"")

# Chafa

## About

Chafa is a command-line utility that converts image data, including
animated GIFs, into graphics formats or ANSI/Unicode character art suitable
for display in a terminal. It has broad feature support, allowing it to be
used on devices ranging from historical teleprinters to modern terminal
emulators and everything in between.

The core functionality is provided by a C library with a public,
well-documented API.

Both library and frontend tools are covered by the Lesser GPL license,
version 3 or later (LGPLv3+).

## Features

- Converts images (including animated GIFs) to terminal-displayable formats
- Supports multiple output formats: ANSI/Unicode character art, Sixel graphics, iTerm2 inline images, Kitty graphics protocol
- Works with various terminal types from historical teleprinters to modern emulators
- Handles multiple image formats as input
- Animation support with customizable playback

## Usage

Basic usage:

```sh
chafa [OPTIONS] [IMAGE...]
```

### Common Options

- `-s, --size <WxH>` - Set output size in character cells
- `-c, --colors <mode>` - Color mode (2, 16, 240, 256, full, etc.)
- `--symbols <symbols>` - Select symbol sets for character art output
- `--format <format>` - Output format (symbols, sixels, kitty, iterm)
- `--animate <on|off>` - Enable/disable animation
- `-d, --duration <seconds>` - Animation duration
- `--bg <color>` - Background color
- `--fg <color>` - Foreground color

### Examples

Convert an image to terminal art:
```sh
chafa image.jpg
```

func checkGlyphFileMagic(path string) bool {
	fi, err := os.Stat(path)
	if err != nil {
		return false
	}
	if fi.IsDir() {
		return false
	}
	if fi.Size() == 0 {
		return false

	if fi.Size() < 4 {
		return false
	}
	f, err := os.Open(path)

	defer f.Close()
	buf := make([]byte, 4)
	n, err := f.Read(buf)

	// TTF: 00 01 00 00
	if buf[0]==0x00 && buf[1]==0x01 && buf[2]==0x00 && buf[3]==0x00 {

	// OTF: OTTO
	if buf[0]=='O' && buf[1]=='T' && buf[2]=='T' && buf[3]=='O' {

	// true, typ1, ttcf
